---
title: "8 · Unsupervised learning"
description: "Finding structure when you have no labels — clustering, PCA, dimensionality reduction — and how far you can trust what you find."
categories: [unsupervised]
---

Sometimes there is no answer key. You have hundreds of CTD profiles and no water-mass
classification, or a community matrix with a hundred taxa and no hypothesis about how
they group. Unsupervised methods look for structure in the data itself.

They are genuinely useful for exploration and for reducing unwieldy data to something
you can plot. They are also the easiest methods to over-read. Clustering algorithms
return clusters whether or not clusters exist; a PCA axis is a mathematical
convenience, not necessarily an ecological gradient.

This section covers the main methods and, just as importantly, the discipline of
interpreting them cautiously.

## In this section

- Clustering
- Principal component analysis
- Dimensionality reduction
- Pattern detection in marine datasets
- Interpretation and limitations of unsupervised methods

::: {.callout-warning}
k-means will happily return five clusters from data with no group structure at all.
Finding clusters is not evidence that clusters exist.
:::
